title: Separate request multiplexor, slot recycler, and cache reconciler to reduce lock contention
creator: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: The serving runtime currently centralizes request multiplexing, slot lifecycle bookkeeping, and KV cache maintenance behind a small set of coarse locks. Under medium-to-high concurrency this leads to tail-latency spikes and CPU stalls observed in p95/p99 flamegraphs. Scope: 1) Extract the request multiplexor into its own async worker with a bounded, lock-free input queue so producers don't contend on the slot allocator. 2) Implement a per-core slot recycler that reclaims slot metadata via MPSC queues and near-zero synchronization. 3) Introduce a cache reconciler background worker responsible for prefix reconciliation and cache tombstone cleanup, instead of doing these synchronously on the hot path. 4) Upgrade runtime dependencies needed for lock-free primitives and async improvements (tokio -> 1.28, crossbeam -> latest compatible, bump parking_lot). Deliverables: - New multiplexor crate (runtime/multiplexor) with clear boundary tests - Slot recycler implementation and microbench harness - Cache reconciler with feature flag (disabled by default) - Dependency upgrade PRs and CI green - End-to-end perf report (latency, throughput, CPU) Acceptance criteria: - p95 latency reduced by >= 15% for the multiplexing-heavy benchmark; p99 reduced by >= 10% - No increase in max RSS or token throughput regressions > 3% - Unit and integration tests for new crates with CI passing - Feature flag allows gradual canary rollout and immediate rollback Risks & mitigations: - Dependency upgrade exposes downstream incompatibilities: create a compatibility shim and keep the old path guarded by feature flag during rollout. - Subtle races in lock-free code: add stress tests, Miri where applicable, and run extended soak in canary. Rollout plan: - Merge multiplexor and recycler behind feature flags -> internal CI/perf runs -> canary in dedicated pool for 48h -> expand to 10% Hosted API -> full rollout if metrics stable. Revert plan: set feature flag to off and redeploy. Test plan: microbench, end-to-end synthetic workload, nightly soak for 72h on staging, and targeted customer workload replay.
